Raj: FYI — noticed a perf regression hitting the chat route this morning, looks token-level. infra alerted at ~02:12 UTC.

perf-bot: automated anomaly detected: metric=token_latency_p95 route=/v1/chat value=86ms (baseline 22ms) start=02:12 UTC severity=warning :rotating_light:

Raj: quick summary from sampling/profiling:
- regression correlates with kernel selector choosing `fp4-opt` for sequences > 512 after last rollout
- KV miss latency (kv_miss_extra_ms) jumped from ~3ms -> ~24ms for affected requests
- batch_wait_ms also increased (median 6ms -> 28ms) for routes with many short-lived sessions

Maya: can you paste the flamegraph snippet and the perf counter dump?

Raj: pasted logs + snippet:```
# top-level hotspots (sampled)
1) attention_kernel_dispatch (38%)
2) wait_for_batch (21%)
3) kv_store_get (14%)
4) token_encode (6%)
```
and a sample trace: `route=/v1/chat seq_len=680 kernel=fp4-opt batch_size=2 token_latency=92ms kv_hit=false`

Liam: hmm — kernel `fp4-opt` reduces compute time for long seqs but seems to cause heavier KV thrashing due to changed memory layout. We should consider two immediate mitigations: 1) pin kernel->fp16 for chat route until we triage, or 2) change kernel selector policy to prefer kernels that preserve KV locality for seq_len range [512,1024].

Sara: we should also instrument a new per-token breakdown metric to catch these earlier. Proposal: `token_latency_{p50,p95,p99}_by_route_and_token_index` (bucketed by token index ranges: 0-32,33-128,129-512,>512).

Maya: agree. Also add a derived SLI: `route_token_latency_burn_rate` computed as: ratio of current token_p95 to baseline_p95 over rolling 15m. Page if burn_rate > 1.5 for 10m with p95 > 50ms.

Raj: draft Prometheus alert rule for review:```yaml
- alert: RouteTokenP95BurnRateHigh
  expr: (avg_over_time(token_latency_p95{route="/v1/chat"}[15m]) / avg_over_time(token_latency_p95_baseline{route="/v1/chat"}[7d:15m])) > 1.5
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "High token p95 burn rate for /v1/chat"
    runbook: "https://redwood/ops/runbooks/token-burn-rate"
```

Liam: small nits: baseline metric `token_latency_p95_baseline` needs explanation (rolling 7d 15m-aligned window) and we need to avoid alerts flapping during deploys. Add a deploy-suppress label or tie into rollout windows.

Sara: paging thresholds we should standardize:
- sev=page: burn_rate > 2.0 for 5m OR p99 token latency > 200ms for 5m
- sev=oncall (notify): burn_rate > 1.3 for 15m

Maya: also add observability panels: per-route KPIs -> tokens/sec, p95 token latency by token-index buckets, batch_wait_ms p95, kv_hit_rate, kernel_selector_ratio (percent of requests picking each kernel). Suggest a compact token-breakdown sparkline per route.

perf-bot: added temporary dashboards: https://dash.redwood/run/abc123 (viewer-only) :white_check_mark:

Raj: action items:
- Raj -> pin chat route kernel to `fp16` for next 2 deploys (roll back selector) (owner: Raj)
- Liam -> add kernel-selector telemetry: kernel_selector_ratio by route + seq_len histogram (ETA 48h)
- Maya -> implement token-index buckets & baseline metric (ETA 72h)
- Sara -> update alert rules and add deploy-suppression logic to paging policy (ETA 24h)
- oncall -> monitor for 2h and escalate if pages fire

oncall: ack'd. I'll watch the pagers and post any notes.

Maya: one more note — add a synthetic check that issues a short-seq and a long-seq request every 5m and records token-level p95; that will catch kernel selector regressions earlier.

Raj: thanks — I'll schedule the kernel pin now and follow up with a short postmortem summary once we have root cause (probably kernel memory layout + kv cache access pattern). :pray:

Liam: if we see KV miss rate remain high after kernel pin, we should consider increasing KV prefetch window and revisiting KV TTL heuristics (owner: Liam).

Sara: tracking issue: https://issues.redwood/INFR-4217

perf-bot: incident-label=investigating, priority=P2

Maya: prepping a quick runbook note for oncall: `if RouteTokenP95BurnRateHigh -> check kernel_selector_ratio, kv_miss_extra_ms, batch_wait_ms, and pin kernel` — will drop in runbook link.

Raj: thank you all.
